question: Why this role? (600 characters max)
posting_quotes: make search fast and keep it fast

claims.text: moved billing from a nightly batch to an event-driven pipeline, a team of 2 engineers
Node.js, PostgreSQL and a message queue

angle: Freshness of data under a latency budget: the billing migration has the same shape.
draft: Proseware's posting asks for someone who can "make search fast and keep it fast". At ExampleCorp I moved our billing service from a nightly batch to an event-driven pipeline with a team of 2 engineers, using Node.js, PostgreSQL and a message queue. The project taught me to measure before optimising, to keep the old path running until the new one had proven itself, and to write down every decision so the next person could follow it. Invoices that used to go out the next morning now go out in minutes. Search has the same shape as that problem: an index that must stay fresh while the data underneath keeps changing, and a latency budget nobody can see until it is blown. I would bring the same habits: a clear migration plan, metrics from day one, and a bias for small reversible steps over a big rewrite.
